QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_11

question.text: A 'Social Impact Fund' referenced in SEBI's SSE framework is registered as which category of Alternative Investment Fund under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012?

answer.text: Category I AIF (sub-category Social Impact Fund / Social Venture Fund).
It is not an AIF at all — it is a separate 'SSE Fund' category notified only by the exchange.

explanation.text: The Logic: The Social Impact Fund (formerly 'Social Venture Fund') is a sub-category of Category I AIF under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012. Category I includes funds that invest in socially or economically desirable sectors (VCFs, Infrastructure Funds, SME Funds, Social Venture/Impact Funds, Angel Funds). These funds issue social units to investors who agree to receive only social returns. The Trap: Option B (PE Cat II) and Option C (Hedge Cat III) are incorrect because both target financial returns; SIFs explicitly accept social-only returns. Option D invents a separate category. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (AIF Ch 1), XIX-B, XIX-C treat Category I AIF directly. V-B (MF Foundation) touches AIF categories peripherally. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When reviewing a SIF that holds ZCZPs issued by your NPO client, check the SIF's scheme documents for the 25% / 100% investable-funds rule — a SIF not exclusively for listed NPOs is capped at 25% NPO exposure, which affects the SIF's attribution of impact to your NPO's program.
